‘Greek Sailors, Atop 3 0- Fo oot ot Mast, } 
Defy Immigration Authorities! 


BALTIMORE, Nov. 1 — (AP); _ 


Three Greek sailors climbed up the 


mast of a freighter today and defied 
the United States government to 
come and get them. 


Immigration officers want to send | 
them back to Greece. The seamen | 
fear they will be sent to prison if | 


they go back. 
A fourth man disappeared ftom 


the ship but police discounted a || 
story that he jumped overboard | 


drowned. 


The three sailors climbed 50 feet 1 
to a vardarm of the freighter Aris- | 


tocratis at 2 o'clock this morning. 


They were still holding out at | 


nightfall. 
What was it all about? 
No Bona Fide Sailors 


When the Aristocratis put in here } 
Oct. 18 from NO6WA Scotia ,with a | 
load of gypsum, four Greek sailors | 
in the crew were “malafied.” This | 


means that an immigration inspec- 
tor decided they were not bona fide 


sailors, that their real purpose was | 
probably to jump ship and sneak | 


into the United States. 


Texas Transport and Terminal | 


company, Inc., local agent for the 


Aristocratis, was warned to detain | 
the four aboard and arrange to get | 


them away from these shores as 
fast as possible. If any of the men 
escaped, Texas Transport would 
have to pay $1,000 apiece. 


John P. Ryan, district enforce- | 


ment officer said he did not know 
why the four men were malafied. 


Maurice Braverman, attorney for | 
them, said he knew why. He | 
charged the immigration service | 


has a black-list supplied by the 
.Greek Maritime Unions (OENO), 


outlawed by Greece in 1947 as a 


Communist organization. 
Says U. S. Went Too Far 


The immigration service won't let | 
any OENO members ashore in the 


United States, Braverman said, 


The government went too far, 
Braverman charged, when it made 
arrangements yesterday with the 
local agents to remove the four 
men from the ship, take them in a 
station wagon to Hoboken, N. J., 
and ship them out today on the 
Neptuna. 


| No one did much to try to get 
them down today. The immigra- 
tion service said it was up to the 
| Steamship agents. The steamship 
| agents declined to talk. Local police 
Said it wasn't any of their. affair.

der that goes up to the sailors’ 
| perch.

to find out which three went up f

\GREEMENT," ON RECOGNIZING THE RED REGIME," HE ADDED A PRESS CONFERENCE.

"ROM THAT OF THE UNITED STATES IN THAT “OUR STAKE IS COMMERCIAL AND 
(THEREFORE BIGGER THAN YOURS, WHICH IS TIED CLOSELY TO YOUR EDUCATORS AND 
MISSIONARIES."

WASHINGTON, NOV “THE JAPANESE=AMERICAN CITIZENS LEAGUE. ‘CAU- 


REMAIN FOR FILING CLAIMS FOR PROPERTY LOSSES. 
yee DEADLINE FOR CLAIMS UNDER THE 1948 EVACUATION CLAIMS ACT IS 

MIKE MASAOKA, LEGISLATIVE DIRECTOR OF THE JsAeCeL. ANTI-DISCRIN- 
INATION COMMITTEE, ADVISED CLAIMANTS TO GET THEIR STATEMENTS OF LOSS 
OF REAL AND PERSONAL PROPERTY TO THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT BY THE END OF 
DECEMBER. 

THE ACT AUTHORIZES THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT TO APPROVE CLAIMS UP TO 
$2,500 FOR PROPERTY LOSSES RESULTING THROUGH NO FAULT OF THEIR OWN 
IN THE EVACUATION OF 110,000 PERSONS OF JAPANESE ANCESTRY FROM THE 
WEST COAST AFTER THE START OF WORLD WAR II. 

CLAIMS EXCEEDING $2,500 MUST BE APPROVED BY CONGRESS. 

MASAOKA SAID IN A STATEMENT THAT SOME OF THE EVACUEES ARE HESI- 
TANT TO FILE CLAIMS BECAUSE OF THE TECHNICALITIES INVOLVED IN 
DETERMINING VALUE OR PROOF OF PROPERTY LOSS. 

"IF IN DOUBT, FILE," MASAOKA ADVISED. 

"IF ONE DOES NOT FILE, THIS MAN MEAN THAT IN THE EVENT IT IS 
EVENTUALLY ESTABLISHED THAT HE DID HAVE A CLAIM IT MAY BE IMPOSSIBLE 
TO RECEIVE COMPENSATION." 

THE JeAeCoL» SAID THE TOTAL VALUE OF REAL AND PERSONAL PROPERTY 
LOSSES BY THE EVACUEES HAS BEEN ESTIMATED FROM $10,000,000 (M) TO 
$100 ,000,000 (M). 

"CONGRESS HAS APPROPRIATED $1,000,000 TO THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT TO 
START PAYING CLAIMS.

The Passion Play dates frgm 1633 


when, an old chronicle says, the 
village of Oberammergau was 
stricken by the plague. Eighty-four 
of the village’s 600 inhabitants went 
to their graves. 

The village elders swore to per- 
form the tragedy of the Passion 
‘every ten years. 

Debates Over Cast Frequent 

The pledge has been carried out 
for 300 years, with only two inter- 
ruptions—the first and second 
world wars. 

Debates over the cast of the Pas- 


“sion Play have been frequent. Vil- 


lage rumor says that in old days, 
the villagers engaged in fist-fights 
when rivalry for the honor grew! 
too hot. 

Alois Lang, a wood-carver and 
hotel proprietor, played the role of. 
Christ in 1934. Then he was de- 


iscribed as the “Austpere Christ.” 
1But he joined the Nazi party, and 


in 1948 went before a de-Nazifica- 
tion court where he was classified 
as the leastalangerous class of Nazi 
and paid the costs of the trial.

young men, Hans Lang, Hugo Rutz 
jand Benedikt Stueckl. The Virgin

DRA, MINN, BELLS RANG TODAY ON A WOODED FARM 
NEAR MORA FOR'A SHY AND SMILING YOUNG MISS FROM TOKYO, JAPAN AND A |. 
MINNESOTA FARM BOY, | 
THE BRIDE WAS 22 YEAR OLD TOSHIE OKUTOMI. THE BRIDEGROOM WAS 
| QBREN LUCHT, ALSO 22, A FORMER MEMBER OF THE U.S. OCCUPATION FORCES 
THEY HAD PLANNED THR WEDDING FOR MORE THAN TWO YEARS BUT 
IMMIGRATION BANS KEPT TOSHIE FROM JOINING ORREN IN MINNESOTA. 
CONGRESS PASSED A SPECIAL ACT TO CLEAR THE WAY, AND TOSHIE ARRIVED 
IN MORA FRIDAY. 
TOSHIE AND ORREN MET ON A RAINY AFTERNOON IN TOKYO. _ 
"SHE STOPPED AND ASKED ME DIRECTIONS," HE SAID. “THEN WHEN IT 
|BEGAN TO RAIN HARD, I BROKE A RULE AND LET HER STAND WITH ME UNDER MY) 
‘SHELTER UNTIL THR RAIN STOPPED." | 
| TOSHIE SPEAKS ENGLISH BUT SHE TALKRD LITTLE TODAY AS 34 GUESTS 
CROWDED THE LIVING ROOM IN THE HOME OF ORREN'S PARENTS, MR. AND 
MRS.ALBERT LUCHT, FOR THE WEDDING. 
THE CEREMONY WAS PERFORMED BY THE REV.OSCAR OLSON, PASTOR OF A 
NEARBY SWEDISH LUTHERAN CHURCH. THE ONLY REMINDER TOSHIE HAD OF HER 


THE CEREMONY WAS PERFORMED BY THE REV.OSCAR OLSON, PASTOR OF A . 
(NEARBY SWEDISH LUTHERAN CHURCH. THE ONLY REMINDER TOSHIE HAD OF HER | 
HOMELAND WAS A JAPANESE LANTERN HANGING FROM THE CEILING ABOVE HER. | 
“ON THE UPRIGHT PIANO WAS A PICTURE OF TOSHIE IN HER JAPANESE KIMONA. 
THE BEST MAN WAS ORREN'S BROTHER, DONALD. THE. BRIDESMAID WAS 
ORREN'’S COUSIN, 17 YEAR OLD EDITH 
THE THRER-TLERED WEDDING CAKE WAS MADE BY ORREN'S AUNT, MRS.EDDIE 
LUCHT. HIS MOTHER PREPARED THE DINNER OF ROAST PORK, POTATOFS, 


VEGETABLES, AND THICK APPLE PIR. | 
ORREN AND TOSHIE ARE GOING TO LIVE ON THE LUCHT 320-ACRE FARM.

Japan Expecting U. S, 
Credit of 100 Million 


TOKYO, Nov. 7 (®)—Grow- 
ing talk of an early Japanese 
peace treaty has led Japan’s 
government to believe it will 
get at least $100,000,000 in long- 
term credit from the United 
States, the newspaper “Asahi” 

“said today. 

“Asahi” said it was generally 
believed here that Treasury 
Secretary John W. Snyder will 
discuss plans for such a loan 
policy with General Douglas 
MacArthur. Mr. Snyder is due 


in Japan next week, H

LONDON, NOV. 7=(AP)=THE TEXT OF A SPEECH TODAY BY MARSHAL 

ALEXANDER M. VASILEVSKY, MINISTER OF RUSSIA'S ARMED FORCES, TO THE 
MOSCOW GARRISON"RS™BROADCAST BY, MOSCOW RADIO AND TRANSCRIBED BY THE 
SOVIET MONITOR." (ABOUT 700) 
_- COMRADE SOLDIERS AND SAILORS, SERGEANTS AND PETTY OFFICERS, COMRADE 
OFFICERS, GENERALS AND ADMIRALS, WORKING PEOPLE OF THE SOVIET UNIONS 

IN THE NAME OF AND ON BEHALF OF THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT AND THE 
CENTRAL COMMITTEE OF THE COMMUNIST PARTY OF THE SOVIET UNION, I GREET 
AND CONGRATULATE YOU ON THE 32ND ANNIVERSARY OF THE GREAT OCTOBER 
SOCIALIST REVOLUTION. THE PEOPLE OF THE SOVIET UNION ARE MARKING THIS 
HISTORIC HOLIDAY BY DECISIVE VICTORIES IN THEIR STRUGGLE FOR THE 
FULFILMENT OF THE POSTWAR STALIN FIVE*YEAR PLAN AHEAD OF TIME, BY 
IMPORTANT ACHIEVEMENTS IN ALL SPHERES OF ECONOMY, CULTURE, SCIENCE AND 
TECHNIQUE. ‘ ACS 

THE MATERIAL WEALTH THAT IS BEING CREATED BY THE SOVIET PEOPLE 
CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVES THE CONDITIONS OF LIFE OF OUR’ PEOPLE, RAISING 
ITS WELL BEING, THE ACHIEVEMENTS OF THE WORKING PEOPLE OF THE SOVIET 


UNION AND THE SOLDIERS OF THE SOVIET ARMED FORCES ARE A VIVID EXPRESSIO 


OF THE WARM AFFECTION OF OUR PEOPLE TO THEIR SOCIALIST MOTHERLAND, 
THEIR BOUNDLESS LOYALTY TO THE SOVIET GOVERNMENT AND THE GREAT 
PARTY OF LENIN AND STALIN. 

WITH EACH NEW STEP OF OUR STATE ON THE ROAD TO COMMUNISM, THE 
WORLD HISTORIC ROLE OF THE TRIUMPH OF THE GREAT OCTOBER REVOLUTION 
IS BEING REVEALED MORE AND MORE CLEARLY. THE ADVANTAGES OF THE 
SOVIET REGIME AS COMPARED WITH THE CAPITALIST REGIME ARE MORE AND 
MORE CONVINCINGLY EXPRESSED. 

UNDER CAPITALISM, INDUSTRIAL PRODUCTION IS AGAIN BEING REDUCED, 
THE STANDARD OF LIVING OF WIDE MASSES OF THE PEOPLE IS BEING SHARPLY 
\LOWERED, MASS UNEMPLOYMENT AND POVERTY ARE GROWING, IRRECONCILABLE 
ECONOMIC AND POLITICAL CONTRADICTIONS ARE GROWING AND BECOMING MORE 
AND MORE ACUTE. THE IMPERIALISTS SEEK TO SOLVE THESE CONTRADICTIONS 
BY A FURTHER ATTACK ON THE LIVING RIGHTS OF THE WORKING PEOPLE, BY 
ENSLAVING AND PUTTING INTO BONDAGE THE FREEDOM-LOVING PEOPLES, BY A 
POLICY OF AGGRESSION AND THE UNLEASHING OF A NEW WAR. 

THE IMPERIALISTS AND WARMONGERS ARE USING ALL THE DARK FORCES 
OF CONTEMPORARY BOURGEOIS SOCIETY, FASCIST PROVOCATEURS, SPIES, 

THEIR LOYAL LACKEYS &lt;= THE RIGHT WING SOCIALISTS AND THE BASE TITO 
GANG.

TO THE MINISTER OF HOME SECURITY, HAS CHARGED THAT BRITAIN IS

WEAPONS "CLEARLY DIRECTED AGAINST THE PEOPLE OF THE SOVIET UNION.

ASSOCIATION FOR THE ADVANCEMENT OF SCIENCE (BAAS), WHICH DROPPED 
HIM AS A MEMBER BECAUSE OF A SPEECH HE MADE TO A MOSCOW RALLY LAST 
AUGUST.

MEMBER OF ITS GOVERNING COUNCIL. IT SAID HE HAD BEEN ASKED FOR AN 
EXPLANATION OF HIS MOSCOW REMARKS AND THAT THE EXPLANATION RECEIVED 
DID NOT REMOVE THE COUNCIL'S OBJECTIONS.

WASHINGTON, NOV 7-CAP)-THE SUPREME COURT HELD TODAY THAT AN AMERI-~- 
CAN-LEASED BASE IS FOREIGN TERRITORY UNDER ONE LAW DESPITE AN EARLIER 
FINDING THAT IT IS A UNITED STATES POSSESSION WHEN ANOTHER LAW IS 
INVOLVED. 

TODAY'S UNANIMOUS OPINION PROMPTED JUSTICE JACKSON TO CHIDE HIS 
COLLEAGUES FOR WHAT HE CALLED "INCONSISTENCY", 

THE TRIBUNAL HELD TODAY THAT THE WIDOW OF’ AN AIRMAN KILLED IN A 


1946 NEWFOUNDLAND CRASH MAY NOT SUE THE UNITED STATES UNDER THE FEDER: 


TORT CLAIMS ACT. 

THAT ACT GIVES U.S. DISTRICT COURTS AUTHORITY TO DECIDE CLAIMS 
AGAINST THE UNITED STATES FOR DAMAGES RESULTING FROM INJURIES AND 
DEATHS. 

JUSTICE REED DELIVERED THE RULING. JUSTICES JACKSON AND FRANKFUR= 
TER WROTE CONCURRING OPINIONS. JUSTICE DOUGLAS TOOK NO PART. 

THE WIDOW, MRS. LILLIAN SPELAR, OF NEW YORK, SOUGHT DAMAGES FOR THE 
DEATH OF HER HUSBAND, MARK SPELAR. HE WAS THE FLIGHT ENGINEER ON AN 
AMERICAN OVERSEAS AIRLINES PLANE WHICH CRASHED OCT. 3, 1946 ON A TAKE= 
OFF FROM HARMON FIELD, NEWFOUNDLAND. ALL ABOARD WERE KILLED. 

HARMON FIELD AND ITS SURROUNDING AREAS IS ONE OF THE BASES LEASED 
BY THE UNITED STATES FROM GREAT BRITAIN IN 1941. MRS. SPELAR CHARGED 
HER HUSBAND'S DEATH WAS DUE TO NEGLIGENCE OF THE GOVERNMENT IN OPERA= 
TION OF THE FIELD. 

SHE SUED IN UeSe DISTRICT COURT IN NEW YORK BUT THE CASE WAS 
DISMISSED ON THE GROUND THE CLAIM AROSE IN A FOREIGN COUNTRY. THE 
UeS. CIRCUIT COURT IN NEW YORK REVERSED THE DISTRICT COURT, HOWEVER. 

THE CIRCUIT COURT CITED AN EARLIER SUPREME COURT RULING THAT A 
U.s.Se-LEASED BASE IN BERMUDA COULD BE CONSIDERED--FOR PURPOSES OF THE 
FAIR LABOR STANDARDS ACTe-A POSSESSION OF THE UNITED STATES. 


THE JUSTICE DEPARTMENT APPEALED TO THE SUPREME COURT FROM THE CIRCUIT 


COURT'S DECISION. 

JUSTICE REED"S OPINION TODAY SAID THE TORT CLAIMS ACT BARS SUITS ON 
CLAIMS WHICH ORIGINATE IN A FOREIGN COUNTRY. 

IN HIS CONCURRING OPINION JACKSON SAID3: 

"TO THOSE UNINITIATED IN THE MODERN METHODS OF STATUTORY CONSTRUC=- 
TION IT MAY SEEM A SOMEWHAT ESOTERIC DOCTRINE THAT THE SAME PLACE AT 


THE SAME TIME MAY LEGALLY BE BOTH A POSSESSION OF THE UNITED STATES AND 


A FOREIGN COUNTRY, 


B74WX 

"THIS DISPARITY RESULTS FROM HOLDING THAT CONGRESS, WHEN IT RE= 
FERS TO OUR LEASED AIRBASES, AT ONE TIME CALLS THEM POSSESSIONS AND AT 
ANOTHER TIME FOREIGN COUNTRIES. WHILE CONGRESSIONAL INCOHERANCE OF 
THOUGHT OR OF SPEECH IS NOT UNCONSTITUTIONAL AND CONGRESS CAN USE A 
CONTRARIETY OF TERMS TO DESCRIBE THE SAME THING, WE SHOULD PAY CON- 
GRESS THE RESPECT OF NOT aa LIGHTLY THAT IT INDULGES IN CON- 


' CHAMBERSBURG, PAs, ARE BEING SHIPPED BY THE COMMERCE INTERNATIONAL 


— 


| COURNSTENCIES OF SPEECH WHICH MAKE THE ENGLISH LANGUAG 
MEANINGLESS 


GRESS THE RESPECT OF NOT ASSUMING LIGHTLY THAT IT INDULGES IN CON- 
CONSISTENCIES OF SPEECH WHICH MAKE THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE ALMOST 
MEANINGLESS." 

JACKSON ADDED THIS CONCLUSIONS 

"THERE IS SOME REASON TO THINK: THE INCONSISTENCY LIES IN THE 
COURT'S RENDERING OF THE STATUTES RATHER THAN IN THE WAY CONGRESS HAS 
WRITTEN THEM." 

FRANKFURTER, WHO ALSO DISSENTED IN THE BERMUDA CASE, JOINED IN JACK- 
SON'S CRITICISM OF THE MAJORITY.

TWO MONTHS OLD TO 55z-ARRIVED BY PLANE TODAY AND FOUND THEMSELVES 
SHORT OF BUS FARE TO :HEIR CALIFORNIA DESTINATION.

B)THE EXTRA MONEY=-AND THREW IN A FREE STEAK DINNER AT THE AIRPORT

© THE ONLY ONE WHO COULD SPEAK ENGLISH, LUBA GORBENKO, 21, SAID 
PS OLDER MEMBERS OF THE SEVEN FAMILIES, ALL CLOSE FRIENDS, HAD LEFT 
PyROSTOV, RUSSIA, ABOUT 18 YEARS AGO, WHEN THE RUSSIANS "WANTED TO 
MAKE COMMUNISTS OF US." 

# SHE SAID THEY MIGRATED TO SEVERAL COUNTRIES, FINALLY SETTLING IN 


TeyERAN AND BECOMING FARMERS,

TPlymouth Art Galleries today were 
"not the usual type of auctiongoer, 
| They were, most of them, poor 
people. They tended to be nervous 
win their gestures and their eyes 
M held dark reservoirs of suspicion. |

» Hitler massacres.

| finger, some 24,000 pieces of silver-| 
i ware confiscated by the Nazis .. .|

Turned Over To IRO 
The silver was captured by Allied 
forces and turned over eventually 
to the International Refugee Or-| 
ganization, which sold it to the | 
gallery for $500,000. Proceeds go to 
help displaced persons. 
Many concentration-camp “alum- 
Ini’ came to see the display. The 
?gailery's owners offered to give

itew were able to do so.

rabbi’s box!’

heirloom—a silver filigreed snuff- 
box inscribed in Hebrew with the 
of her husband's father. 
Wife, 7 Children Died

covered a tray and fourteen silver 
cordial-cup holders inscribed with

feel much better.”

‘Firebird’ Can Be Launched| 
From One Plane At Another 


San Diego, Cak, Nov. 13 (®)— 
The “firebird,” 2 rocket-powered | 
‘target-seeking missile with a prox- 
imity fuse for launching from one 
iplane ageinst another, has been) 
developed experimentally for the| 
‘Air Force. 
Com-| 
jpany announced this today after) 
flight tests with the missile, first} 
of its kind for the Air Force. 

The “firebird.” also known as 
the XAAM-A-1, is small enough to 


permit a jet fighter to carry sev- 


eral. It is intended for use against 


‘ian enemy plane hidden by dark- 


iness or clouds. 

The “firebird” was described as} 
ja little ever 6 inches in diameter 
and about 10 feet long. It can be 
‘hung on ordinary external bomb 
racks. 


Uses Booster Rocket 

Upon launching, a booster rocket 
gives the missile a push to its high 
cruising speed. This 30-inch boost- 
ler is then blown off, and rocket 
imotors in the middle take over for 


flight to the target. 


| The missile has electronic equip- 
ment for locating its victim and 
for guiding its flight to at least a 
mear collision. The proximity fuse, 
developed during the recent war, 
will detonate the missile’s explosive 
charge on approaching the target,

er around Bermuda.

Newfoundland.

was 95 airmen. also set by a mili-! 
tary air transport 
master on a flight between Mobile|

JS. SPURNS MEYERS 
ON $50,000 OFFER 


Washington, Nov. 17 (A. P.).— 
The Government has turned down 


an offer by former Major- ‘Gen, 


Bennett E. Meyers to settle all 
the wartime tax claims against 
him for about $50,000 cash. 

It included a proposition that 
the former Air Force purchasing| 
chief, now in prison and seeking! 
parole, would plead guilty to 
single misdemeanor count in con- 
nection with income tax-filings’ 
if the Justice Department“would| 
drop projected,. prosecu- 
tions. 

An incomé tax misdemeanor 
carries a maximum sentence of 
one year, whereas a felony is pun- 
ishable by as much as five years 
in prison. 

The Justice Department and 
the Internal Revenue - Bureau 
have declined to discuss the pro- 
posed settlement, 

The exact amount of Meyers’s 
tax liabilities is in dispute, bu 
Government sources, concedin 
the possibility of overlaps an 
duplications, have estimated tha 
it might run as high as $400,000. |

came Under Secretary of the Navy.)

agencies, including the Air Force.) 
| Volunteered For Duty

of research and experimental work

‘before Pearl Harbor and was ap-

assigned first to a submarine chaser) 
early i: 1943.

other submarine chaser and sent to 
the Mediterranean, where his craft! 
served through the later stages of| 
the North African operation and| 
then sailed to Salerno and Sicily.

AP SPECIAL WASHINGTON SERVICE (440) 
WASHINGTON, NOV.18=CAP)-REP.MCSWEENEY (D-OHIO) SAYS A THREE MONTHS 


TOUR OF EUROPE HAS CONVINCED HIM THE MARSHALL PLAN IS PAYING DIVIDENDS 


IN THE FORM OF WEAKENED COMMUNIST INFLUENCE IN WESTERN EUROPE. 
"IT IS DIFFICULT TO MEASURE THE TANGIBLE EFFECTS OF A PROGRAM SUCH 
AS THE MARSHALL PLAN," MCSWEENEY TOLD A REPORTER. “BUT I DID SEE 
TANGIBLE EVIDENCE OF A DEFINITE DECLINE IN COMMUNIST STRENGTH IN THE 
"COMMUNIST REVERSES IN THEIR ELECTIONS, ESPECIALLY IN AUSTRIA, WHO 
THAT, AND I GIVE MUCH OF THE CREDIT TO THE MARSHALL PLAN." 
MCSWEENEY'* S TOUR CARRIED HIM THROUGH IRELAND, WHERE HE KISSED THE 
BLARNEY STONE, AND INTO ENGLAND, FRANCE, GERMANY, AUSTRIA AND ITALY. 


THE CONGRESSMAN SAID HE COULD SPEAK WITH MOST AUTHORITY ABOUT ITALYs| 


A COUNTRY IN WHICH HE SPENT A YEAR AND A HALF AS CHIEF OF THE WELFARE 
DIVISION OF THE U.S. MILITARY GOVERNMENT AND A YEAR AS FOREIGN REPRE@= 
SENTATIVE OF AMERICAN RELIEF FOR ITALY AFTER THE WAR. 

"WHEN THE MARSHAJ.L PLAN WAS BEING DEBATED, ITS OPPONENTS DEMANDED 
TO KNOW WHETHER WE EVER COULD END IT, AND WHETHER WE WOULD BE ANY BET- 
BER IF WE DID QUIT," MCSWEENEY SAID. 

"THE ITALIANS ARE TRYING TO PREPARE THEMSELVES FOR THE END OF THE 
ECONOMIC AID PROGRAM NOW SCHEDULED FOR 1952. 
WILL HAVE GOTTEN BY THEN, BUT THEY ARE TRYING. 

"THEY ARE TRYING TO STRENGTHEN THEIR TAX SYSTEM. 

"THEY ARE TRYING TO WORK OUT AN AGRARIAN PROGRAM TO STABILIZE THEIR 


"THEY ARE DOING A STARTLING JOB OF RECONSTRUCTION WITH NOT ENOUGH 


MATERIALS. 
"THEY USE STONES AS THEY WERE USED IN THE DAYS OF CAESAR TO REBUILD 


WAR=RUINED BRIDGES, AND IT*S A HEARTBREAKING TASK. 
"BUT WITHOUT ENOUGH STEEL, THEY HAVE TO DO THE BEST THEY CAN, 
AND ARE DOING IT." 
MCSWEENEY SAID HE CONSIDERS FASCIST ELEMENTS IN ITALY STILL ARE 
A MENACE, BUT THAT "THEY ARE LYING LOW NOW, HOPING THE COMMUNISTS WILL 


EXPEND THEMSELVES." 
COMMUNISM, HE SAID, IS LOSING STRENGTH IN ITALY “UNDER THE WISE 


GOVERNMENT OF PREMIER ALCIDE DE GASPERI." 


B26WxX (Q) 
THE OHIOAN PRAISED THE WORK OF MARSHALL PLAN STAFF WORKERS IN 


EUROPE. HE SAID HE IS SUSPICIOUS OF CRITICS WHO CONTEND THE PORGRAM 
IS LESS EFFECTIVE THAN IT SHOULD BE, ESPECIALLY WHEN THE CRITICS ARE 
EUROPEANS. 

"EUROPE OF COURSE WANTS TO BEAT DOWN OUR TARIFFS, AND THAT’S A 
FORM OF PROPAGANDA THEY USE TO HELP THEIR CAUSE,” MCSWEENEY SAID. 

"BUT WE NEED TO PROTECT OUR INDUSTRIES AND OUR HIGH STANDARDS, 
AND THEY SHOULD REMEMBER THAT WITHOUT THESE STANDARDS WE COULD NEVER 
AFFORD TO HELP THEM.” | 

THE CONGRESSMAN SAID THAT IN ALMOST EVERY COUNTRY HE VISITED HE 
FOUND FRIENDS-=-FELLOW CONGRESSMEN TOURING THE CONTINENT AND BRITAIN 


OFFICIAL MISSIONS.

LAKE SUCCESS, NOV. 18=(AP)=GORDON CLAPP'"S UNITED NATIONS SURVEY 
MISSION TODAY URGED ESTABLISHMENT OF A LARGE-SCALE INTERNATIONAL 
PUBLIC WORKS PROGRAM IN THE MIDDLE EAST TO REHABILITATE SOME 750,000 
ARAB REFUGEES UPROOTED BY THE PALESTINE WAR. THE SUGGESTED PROJECT 
JOULD BE ALONG THE LINES OF THE AMERICAN WPA AND PWA OF THE 1950S. 


THE MISSION HEADED B P ON LEAVE AS BOARD CHAIRMAN OF THE © 
ITY, STRESSED ‘ : NEEDED IN THE NEXT 18 MONTHS TO LIQUIDATE THE RELIEF PROGRAM AND CARRY|

TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY, STRESSED THAT A NEW APPROACH TO THE 
PROBLEM AS NEEDED. ITS REPORT SAID: "THE FORMULA IS MORE WORK AND 


IMPROVEMENT PROJECT 
SEVERAL TYPES OF PROJECTS WOULD BE INSTITUTED IN WADI ZERQA, NORTH 
OF THE HASHEMITE JORDAN CAPITAL OF AMMAN, TO DEVELOP THE WHOLE AREA 
AS A COMPLETE UNIT. THE REPORT SAID A CENTRALLY LOCATED VILLAGE 
SHOULD BE MADE PART OF THE SCHEME THERE "TO PROVIDE ADEQUATE HOUSING 
FACILITIES FOR THE TEMPORARY REFUGEE CONSTRUCTION WORKERS." 

U.N. DELEGATIONS STUDIED THE REPORT, BUT WERE RESERVED IN THEIR 
COMMENTS ON IT. SOME SAID THEY NEEDED MORE TIME TO CONSIDER ITs 
IMPLICATIONS. 

THE MISSION POINTED OUT THAT REPATRIATION OF THE ARABS TO HOMES 
Now IN ISRAELI TERRITORY WOULD REQUIRE POLITICAL DECISIONS IT IS 
(OT COMPETENT TO MAKE. IT POINTED OUT THAT ISRAEL HAS OFFERED TO

SETTLEMENT OF ALL OTHER ISSUES. 

THE MISSION SAID "USEFUL, GAINFUL EMPLOYMENT CAN X X X BE FOUND 
FOR ALL THE REFUGEES ABLE AND WILLING TO WORK."

DIRECT RELIEF PROGRAM BE CUT FROM 940,000 TO 652,000 BY THE END 
OF THE YEAR. IT SAID: 

"THERE IS NO DOUBT THAT RATIONS GREATLY IN EXCESS OF THE NUMBER 
JUSTIFIABLE WITHIN THE ORIGINAL INTENTIONS OF THE GENERAL ASSFMBLY 
OF THE UNITED NATIONS HAVE BEEN AND ARE BEING ISSUED." 

THE MISSION EXPLAINED THAT THOUSANDS OF PERSONS IN ARAB COUNTRIES 
ARE GETTING RELIEF WHO ARE NOT ENTITLED TO IT. THE BULK OF THESE 
CASES, THE REPORT SAID, INVOLVE REFUGEES WHO ARE EMPLOYED OR NEEDY 
PERSONS WHO ARE NOT REFUGEES AT ALL.

COMMISSION. ITS REPORT WAS SENT HERE FROM HEADQUARTERS AT BEIRUT,

IT IS CLEAR THAT THE RESOLUTIONS NOW BEFORE THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY 
RESULT OF A LONG AND ARDUOUS EFFORT AT COMPROMISE. FOR THIS 
THEY OUGHT NOT TO BE PRESENTED TO THE WORLD AS FULLY SATISFY- 
REQUIREMENTS OF JUSTICE AND FAIR=DEALING AMONG NATIONS. 

THE FORMULA FOR LIBYA RECOMMENDED BY THE COMMITTEE IS PRE*EMINENTLY 
SATISFACTORY. IT PROVIDES FOR INDEPENDENCE IN TWO YEARS. IT ONLY 
REMAINS FOR THE ASSEMBLY TO MAKE IT PLAIN ON THE RECORD, DEYOND ANY 


5 
fii 


MISUNDERSTANDING THAT MAY ARISE AS A RESULT OF VERBAL HAIR@SPLITTING, 
THAT IT IS OUR DESIRE TO SEE ESTABLISHED ONE INDEPENDENT AND SOVEREIGN 
STATE OF LIBYA, LEAVING IT TO THE INHABITANTS TO DETERMINE THEIR OWN 
FORM OF GOVERNMENT, INCLUDING THE NATURE AND DEGREE OF UNION BEST 
SUITED "AND MOST ACCEPTABLE TO THEMSELVES. 

WITH RESPECT TO THE COMMITTEE'S RECOMMENDATION ON ITALIAN 
SOMALILAND, EVERYONE HERE IS AWARE OF THE DIFFICULT COMPRONISES 
EMBOIDIED THEREIN X X X THERE IS, FIRST OF ALL, THE UNCONTROVERTED FACT 
THAT A SIZEABLE AND ARTICULATE SECTION OF THE INHABITANTS OF THE TERR= 
ITORY IS VIOLENTLY OPPOSED TO THE RETURN OF ITALYe THERE, ALSO, 

IS THE PROFOUND CONCERN REPEATEDLY EXPRESSED BY THE ETHIOPIAN DELEG- 
ATION TO THE EFFECT THAT THE SECURITY OF ETHIOPIA WOULD BE ENDANGERED 
PY THE RETURN OF A FORMER AGGRESSOR TO A TERRITORY ADJOINING HER 
PORDERS. THERE, FINALLY, IS THE CONSIDERATION THAT THE PROPOSAL FOR 
DIRECT UNITED NATIONS TRUSTEESHIP OVER THIS TERRITORY WAS REJECTED 
SOLELY ON THE UNVERIFIED THESIS THAT IT IS IMPRACTICABLE, THOUGH ITS 
LEGAL AND MORAL BASIS HAS NEVER BEEN SERIOUSLY QUESTIONED BY ANYONE, 

THESE ARE CONSIDERATIONS OF THE GRAVEST KIND, AND THE RECOMMENDAT- 
IONS OF THE COMMITTEE MUST BE VIEWED IN THE REVEALING LIGHT OF THE 


MISGIVINGS THAT HAVE BEEN EXPRECSED, BECAUSE THESE

created parliament as the official 
executive body. 

Article 5 fixed a regular time 
of meeting.

TELAVIA, ISRAEL, NOV. 22-(AP)-A FORMER HIGH-RANKING ISRAELI 
OFFICER WAS GIVEN A "SYMBOLIC SENTENCE" OF ONE DAY IN PRISON TODAY 
FOR HIS PART IN ORDERING THE EXECUTION DURING THE PALESTINE WAR OF 
MIER TOBIANSKY, WHO WAS LATER PROVED INNOCENT. 

THE OFFICER WAS ISSER BEERI, THE ISRAELI ARMY’S CHIEF INTELLIGENCE 
OFFICER, WHO WAS FOUND GUILTY OF MANSLAUGHTER. 

THE "SYMBOLIC SENTENCE" WAS HANDED DOWN ON THE GROUNDS THAT BEERI 
AND THE THREE COURT MARTIAL JUDGES HE APPOINTED IN THE FIELD TO TRY 
—— ACTED IN GOOD FAITH, CONSIDERING THE HECTIC WARTIME 

TOBIANSKY, A VETERAN EMPLOYE OF THE JERUSALEM ELECTRIC 
CORPORATION, WAS EXECUTED ON CHARGES OF HAVING TURNED OVER A LIST OF 
JEWISH ELECTRICITY USERS TO MICHAEL BRYANT, ONE-TIME DIRECTOR OF THE 
CORPORATION. | 

BRYANT WAS SUSPECTED OF CONTACTING THE ARABS, THUS ENABLING THEM TO 
PINPOINT ARTILLERY FIRE ON VITAL ARMS FACTORIES AND OTHER 
INSTALLATIONS IN JEWISH-HELD JERUSALEM. 

A TEL AVIV COURT LAST JULY FOUND, AFTER LENGTHY INVESTIGATION, 
THAT TOBIANSKY HAD ACTED IN GOOD FAITH IN HANDING OVER THE LIST. 

IT WAS ALSO DISCLOSED THAT THE LIST WAS HANDED OVER FIVE DAYS AFTER 
THE ARAB SHELLING ENDED DURING THE FIRST TRUCE.

BOSTON, NOVe 23=¢AP)-HAD GUADALCANAL FALLEN TO THE JAPANESE, A YEAR 


WOULD HAVE BEEN ADDED TO THE WAR IN THE PACIFIC. 


SO SAID HARVARD HISTORIAN SAMUEL ELIOT MORISON TODAY IN AN bpd 
DEPARTMENT SA 


WHICH EXPLAINED WHY HE HAS DEVOTED AN ENTIRE VOLUME--"THE STRUGGLE FOR 
GUADALCANAL®"=-TO THE SIX MONTHS CAMPAIGN FOR THAT “STINKING ISLAND." - 
THE VOLUME, FIFTH OF HIS PROJECTED 14-VOLUME HISTORY OF THE NAVY IN 
WORLD WAR II, WAS PUBLISHED TODAY BY LITTLE, BROWN &amp; CO. 


CAPT.MORISON=-HE WAS COMMISSIONED BY THE NAVY AND ASSIGNED TO WRITE fe 


THE HISTORY=-GAVE SEVERAL REASONS WHY GUADALCANAL WAS HELD. FIRST OF 
ALL WAS THE UNFLINCHING COURAGE OF THE INITIAL INVADING FORCE OF 
MARINES, LATER AUGMENTED BY ARMY UNITS. THEN CAME A SERIES OF SIX 
NAVAL BATTLES UNPRECEDENTED IN FEROCITY. FOUR WERE NIGHT GUNFIRE 
ACTIONS "OF A KIND WE MAY NEVER SEE AGAIN," THE HISTORIAN SAID. 
"COSTLY THEY WERE, TOO, BOTH IN SHIPS AND IN MEN,” HE RELATES.» 
MAY SEARCH THE SEVEN SEAS IN VAIN FOR AN OCEAN GRAVEYARD WITH 


OF SO MANY SHIPS AND SAILORS AS THAT BODY OF WATER BETWEEN GUADALCANAL, \ 
SAVO AND FLORIDA ISLANDS WHICH OUR BLUEJACKETS CALLED IRONBOTTOM SOUND." 


MORISON PULLED NO PUNCHES IN DISCUSSING THE BATTLE OF SAVO ISLAND-- 
"PROBABLY THE WORST BEATING THE UNITED STATES EVER TOOK." 

"THERE ARE NO ALIBIS," HE SAID. "SO MANY PEOPLE MADE SO MANY MIS- 
TAKES, YOU CAN'T HANG ANYONE FOR IT.® 

IN THAT BATTLE, THE UeSe CRUISERS VINCENNES, QUINCY AND ASTORIA AND 
THE AUSTRALIAN CRUISER CANBERRA WERE LOST, WITH MORE THAN 1,000 KILLED 
AND 700 WOUNDED, AND A CUP OF TEA WAS PARTLY RESPONSIBLE. 

AN AUSTRALIAN SEARCH PLANE SIGHTED THE JAP FORCES AT 10 O'CLOCK IN 
THE MORNING, BUTs “THE PILOT INSTEAD OF BREAKING RADIO SILENCE, OR 


RETURNING TO BASE, WHICH HE COULD HAVE DONE IN TWO HOURS, SPENT MOST ore nO 


THE AFTERNOON COMPLETING HIS SEARCH MISSION, CAME DOWN AT MILNE BAY, | 
HAD HIS TEA AND THEN REPORTED THE CONTACT." 
LOST BEFORE THE VITAL INFORMATION REACHED THE ALLIED FLAGSHIP. 
"THE NAVY DID VERY WELL," SAID MORISON, “WHEN IT HAD ITS OWN AIR.” 
AT ONE CRUCIAL PHASE IN THE CAMPAIGN, MORISON CREDITS THE CARRIER . 
ENTERPRISE, AND ADMIRAL WILLIAM F.HALSEY WHO DISPATCHED HERE, WITH 
SAVING GUADALCANAL AND ITS VITAL HENDERSON FIELD. IT WAS A DIFFICULT 


DECISION TO MAKE.

Steel nationalization promises to 
be a major issue when the elections 
come at the end of the Laborites’ 
five-vear terms. 

Conservative party leader Win- 
ston Churchill, Britain's wartime 
Prime Minister, has declared that 
the elections, among other things, 


will be a virtual “referendum” on 


the steel nationalization issue. 
Churchill, campaigning now for 
re-election of the Government’s 
leadership, has promised to repeal 
the bill if his Conservatives win. 


Compromise Puts It Off 


The Lords have blocked passage 
of the bill until now, even though 


the predominantly Labor House of 


Commons passed it. The Lords said 
it should be left open as an issue 
in the next election. 

The Labor party compromised 
with the Lords, setting back the 
date of take over from May 1, 1950.) 
which they had originally demand- 
ed, in exchange for passage of the 
bill. 

Passage of the nationalization} 
bill will, therefore, be one of the 
major campaign points for the 
Laborites, who can now point out 
that they have fulfilled all of their 
legislative promises. 

Willing To Delay Action 

By recently cutting the veto) 
powers of the House of Lords the) 
Labor Government could have| 
overriden their objection to the} 
state ownership bill. But the Labor-| 
ites maintained it would have been} 
physically impossible to take over! 


the industry technically by May 1h 


anyway, so they were willing to! 
accept the delay and make the bill 
an election issue.

clude coal mining, electricity pro-

and the Bank of England.

Western Allies Define 


Scope Bonn Pact 


Bonn, Germany. Nov. 25 
The Allies made it clear today that 
the agreement they signed with 
the West German Federal Govern- 
ment is not to be regarded “as a 
steppingstone for further de. 
mands.” 

In a news conference. the Allied 
high commissioners said ne gotia- 
tions with Federal Chancellor Kon.- 
rad Adenauer were complete. 

The agreement relaxing occupa- 
lion controls signed yesterday 
would stand until the occupation 
statute is reviewed in the autumn 
of next vear, they said. 

The news conference was con- 
ducted hy Sir*“Brian Robertson. 
United Kingdom high commission- 
er: M. Andre Francois-Poncet 
French high commissioner. and 
Maj. Gen. George P. Hays. deputy 
American high commissioner. 
American High Commissioner John 
J. McCloy was in London. 

Triple Purpose 

General Robertson, reading a 
Statement on behalf of the three 
allies. said the agreement sought to 
do things: 

To promote the prestige and | 
Pid of the West German | 


| Federal Gevermmaal, “That is 
| why we have proceeded by free 
discussions instead of a dictate,” 
Robertson said. 


2. To reintroduce Germany into 
international political society. 

3. To remove causes of friction 
between the occupying powers 
and the German people. 

Robertson said the chief causes | 

of friction have been dismantling 
and restrictions on shipbuilding. 
“May Be Impossible” 
Robertson said: “It cannot be 
easy and may be impossible to re- 
;move all causes of friction between | 
,the occupying and the occupied.” 
The high commissioners felt that 
jthey had made a generous contri-’ 
bution and had held back nothing 
except on considerations of strict! 
security, he said. 
“We recognize that the Federal 
iGovernment has made a notable 
contribution also,” he continued, 
“We trust that thereby the way has 
been made smooth in that between 
now and the time for the review of 
the occupation statute there may be 
a steady progress and evolution 
without contention meanwhile.”

BOSTON, NOV .27=(AP)=HENRY. AWALLACE SAID TODAY DAYS OF THE 
COLD. WAR ARE DRAWING TO A CLOSE AND THE ONLY QUESTION IS WHETHER IT 
ae BE SUCCEEDED BY HOT WAR, DEPRESSION OR A VIGOROUS APPROACH TO 

ACE." 

“IN YEAR FIVE OF THE ATOMIC BONB ERA,® HE SAID, 
TOLERATE THE LUXURY OF HALFWAY MEASURES. WE MUST. BEGIN TO WAGE PEACE 
AS ENTHUSIASTICALLY AS WE WAGED WAR IN 1944. 

"THIS DOESN'T MEAN COMMUNISM, OR EVEN SOCIALISM," WALLACE SAID IN 
AN ADDRESS AT COMMUNITY CHURCH. 

"BUT IT DOES MEAN A NEW KIND OF CAPITALISM WHICH IS WILLING TO COME 
TO AN UNDERSTANDING WITH RUSSIA AND ENGAGE IN JOINT PLANNING WITH 
GOVERNMENT TO SERVE THE GENERAL WELFARE OF HUMANITY IN BOTH THE UNITED 
STATES AND THE WORLD.* 

WALLACE SAID THE AMERICAN WORKER IS "STILL VERY CONSERVATIVE ON 
EVERY SUBJECT EXCEPT HIS OWN WAGES. X X X UNTIL HE IS UNEMPLOYED THE 
AVERAGE AMERICAN WILL BE SLOW TO RESPOND TO THOSE WHO ASK HIM TO LOOK 
BENEATH THE SURFACE. 

"HE WILL EVEN BACK THE TRUMAN DOCTRINE AND THE NORTH ATLANTIC 
MILITARY PACT UNTIL HE IS CONVINCED THAT HE CAN GET MORE EMPLOYMENT 
SOME OTHER WAY.® 

THERE IS, HE SAID, “JUST ONE ROAD TO PEACEFUL PROSPERITY AND THAT 
IS THE ROAD OF DEVELOPING THE BACKWARD AREAS OF THE WORLD THROUGH THE 
UNITED NATIONS, REGARDLESS OF IDEOLOGY."

Plan for Atomic ‘Breeding.’ 


Hafstad said the AEC’s Ar- 
gonne National Laboratory at 
Chicago has completed the “nu- 
clear design” for breeding atomic 
materials. 

“Breeding” would mean great- 
ly expanded resources of atomic 
materials for use in bombs or as 
‘fuels in established or proposed 
peacetime applications of atomic 
energy. It would mean that in 
,the production of these materials 
full use could be made of ura- 
nium-238, the non-fissionable kind 
that is 140 times more plentiful 
‘in nature than scarce uranium. 
235, the “fissionable” kind.

could be made of the non-fission- 
jable metal thorium, which is even? 
‘more plentiful than U-238 A

jleasing atomic energy.

It is assumed that much of the 
increased power of the later model 
hombs arises from improvements in| 


efficiency of the nuclear explosion | 
jrather than radically different 
j bomb mechanism. The refinement 
(of the explosive material itself, as 
/well as retarding devices to prevent 


a relative slow reaction before the 
full hursting effect is attained with- 


in the bomb casing, probaDly has 
been aimed at. 

One of the first things the nue] 
lear scientists found out in the &amp; 


first experiments in the New Mex- &amp; 
ico laboratory and testing ground | 


was that the amount of energy re- # 


leased in the uranium then used | 
corresponded to utilization of onty § 
about one-tenth of one per cent of | 
the mass, This means that improve- } 
ment of only a fraction of a per] 
ent in efficiency would produce a} 
vastly more effective explosion. 
The early bomb developers also] 
were confronted with the fact that } 
they were limited to a bomb con-| 
taining a definite amount of ex-| 
plosive material. Less than the] 
“critical” amount wouldn't explode | 
when the segments were brought 
suddenly together; too much pro-§ 
duced a premature reaction. bs

MRS. MADSEN, 22-YEAR OLD BROOKLYN BEAUTY, CRIED SILENTLY 
THROUGHOUT THE HEARING. HER HUSBAND, LT. ANDREW E.MADSEN OF 
OAKLAND, CALIF., WAS SHOT TO DEATH WITH A SERVICE PISTOL IN

BETWEEN HER AND ANOTHER WOMAN AT A PARTY IN THE HOME OF FRIENDS.

COURT TO COMMIT MRS. MADSEN FOR A MENTAL EXAMINATION, BUT THE 
COURT REJECTED THE MOTION. 

®COUNSEL FOR THE DEFENSE HAS SUGGESTED THAT INSANITY MIGHT BE 
INTEPPOSED AS A DEFENSE," JOHNSON SAID. 
PROCEEDING WITH THE CASE, THE MENTAL CAPACITY OF THE ACCUSED, 
SHOULD BE DETERMINED.®

THE MOTION. THE COURT REJECTED IT IN GROUNDS THAT JOHNSON DID 
NOT ALLEGE INSANITY, BUT SAID MERELY THAT INSANITY MIGHT BE USED 
AS A DEFENSE.

WASHINGTON, NOV.30@(AP)-WHERE DOES REP.J.PARNELL THOMAS (RONJ) 
AS TO HIS SEAT IN THE HOUSE» NOW THAT HE HAS DECIDED ACAINST FIGHTING 


S A CHARGE OF DEFRAUDING THE GOVERNMENT? 
HE STILL HOLDS IT. BUT HE COULD RESIGN OR THE HOUSE COULD THROW 


HIM OUT. 

THERE IS A PRECEDENT FOR RESIGNING, BUT THOMAS DOES NOT HAVE TO 
FOLLOW IT. IN 1926, JOHN WeLANGLEY, A KENTUCKY REPUBLICAN, GAVE UP 
HIS HOUSE SEAT AFTER HE HAD BEEN CONVICTED IN HIS HOME STATE. AVAIL- 
ABLE RECORDS HERE DO NOT SHOW THE CHARGE AGAINST LANGLEY. : 

THOMAS TODAY WITHDREW A WOT GUILTY PLEA TO CHARGES OF PADDING 
HIS OFFICE PAYROLL AND THRE HIMSELF ON THE MERCY OF THE COURT. HE 
REFUSED AFTERWARDS TO TALK ABOUT HIS FUTURE PLANS. 

THE HOUSE HAS THE POWER TO OUST ANY OF ITS MEMBERS. IT IS THE 
SOLE JUDGE OF THEIR QUALIFICATIONS--NOT THE COURTS. BUT NOT SINCE 
CIVIL WAR DAYS HAS A HOUSE MEMBER BEEN EXPELLED, 

IN 1919, VICTOR L.BERGER, A SOCIALIST FROM WISCONSIN, WAS ELECTED 
TO THE HOUSE BUT WAS REFUSED A SEAT. HE WAS UNDER INDICTMENT FOR A 
FEDERAL OFFENSE AND WAS CONVICTED AND SENTENCED TO PRISON. 

THE SUPREME COURT REVERSED THE CONVICTION IN 1921 AND BERGER WAS 
AGAIN ELECTED TO THE HOUSE. THIS TIME HE WAS ALLOWED TO TAKE THE OATH 
AND SERVED SEVERAL TERNS. 

THE MAIN DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE BERGER AND LANGLEY CASES AND THE 
THOMAS CASE IS THAT THE ALLEGED OFFENSES AGAINST BERGER AND LANGLEY 
OCCURED PRIOR TO ELECTION. THE CHARGES AGAINST THOMAS INVOLVE HIS 


S ACTIONS WHILE A MEMBER OF THE HOUSE. 


JAMES M.CURLEY, MASSACHUSETTS DEMOCRAT, WAS CONVICTED ON MAIL 
FRAUD CHARGES WHILE A MEMBER OF THE HOUSE, BUT HIS CASE WAS NOT 
FINALLY SETTLED IN HIGHER COURTS UNTIL AFTER HIS TERM EXPIRED. 

ANDREW J.MAY (D-KY) WAS INDICTED ON WARTME BRIBERY CHARGES WHILE 
= A MEMBER OF THE HOUSE BUT WAS NOT CONVICTED UNTIL AFTER HE WAS 

DEFEATED FOR RE-ELECTION,
